rv.q: For all the liveliness of the eight performers and the richness of Young’s Scots-language text, there’s a too frequent settling for melodramatic cliche at the expense of dramatic development that results in characters and relationships feeling incomplete (including scenes showing how Chris’s choices are affected by sexual violence).
In short, it’s a triumph, to be sought out whether you know the novel or not.
With directon from Finn den Hertog, this is a visually stunning adaptation of Lewis Grassic Gibbon’s classic novel
Morna Young's stunning adaptation uses the lyricism of old Scots, with its blunt Doric beauty and mystery, to create an impressionistic tableau of heartbreak and hope.
It's a solid production, but it "needs to dig deeper" to uncover the heart of this very human drama.
For all its bold ambition, by trying to cram too much in, this production of Sunset Song fails to capture the thematic complexities of the original.
